result.title: Simulating Training Spikes of Deep Neural Networks by Layer-wise Random Feature Models
result.summary: Intermittent ``spikes'' in loss, during the pre-training of Large Language Models (LLMs), remains a mysterious phenomenon both theoretically and empirically. In this paper, we show that simple quadratic models with heavy-tailed, power-law distributed inputs can replicate these spikes. We introduce a theoretical framework and simulation algorithm to model per-layer training dynamics of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), using such quadratic models. In a case study on an Adam hyperparameter configuration (where $β_2$ is set close to $1$) known to induce spikes in Transformer LMs, our simulation successfully predicts bumps indicating spiky behavior from a given checkpoint. Furthermore, we derive an appropriate $β_2$ schedule from observed metrics, which empirically improves performance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用带重尾幂律输入的二次模型与逐层随机特征模拟，复现并预测 Transformer 预训练中的 loss spike，并从观测指标推导 Adam β2 调度以提升性能。
